course_name_original: Cálculo, Diseño y Simulación de Sistemas de Control
course_name_en: Calculation, Design and Simulation of Control Systems
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of dynamic systems analysis (familiarity with transfer function concepts and frequency response/Bode diagrams)
Familiarity with MATLAB mathematical software for engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study.
Students possess the learning skills that will allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.

To elaborate technical specifications that allow to pose a problem in mechatronic engineering maintaining a global and integrative vision and using prescriptive, procedural or performance specifications as appropriate.
To organize conceptual design activity to support decision making and selection among possible solutions to an engineering problem.

To know and use finite element simulation software to study the integral behavior (mechanical, static and dynamic, thermal, magnetic, electrical, etc.) of mechatronic elements and correctly interpret the results.
To select the most appropriate programmable logic devices in each case for the design of mechatronic systems, manage their development systems and design the interface stages that may be necessary.
To incorporate the necessary electric, hydraulic and pneumatic sensors and actuators according to the characteristics of the mechatronic system, its specifications and its integration with it.
To design control systems of different complexity, from simple loops to distributed systems.
To discriminate the most critical components in a mechatronic system and justify their possible redesign from the point of view of the control system.
To fundamentedly justify the different options for the automation of a mechatronic machine or technological process.
Acquire knowledge on modeling of physical systems oriented to the control of mechatronic systems.
Decide the design specifications of the control system.
Decide the type of controller appropriate to the specifications.
Evaluate the performance and limitations of a control system.
Apply the definition of sensitivity to calculate the variation of control system behavior due to parameter variations.

Plot sensitivity functions in Matlab and analyze the behavior of a control system in terms of reference tracking, disturbance rejection, robustness, relative stability, and robust stability (against model variations).

Know and be able to carry out alternative control system designs using specific solutions and architectures (reference pre-filtering, feedforward, cascade, anti-windup structures, gain scheduling control, etc.).

assessment_rules: For ordinary assessment, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required for both EV1 (written exams) and EV2 (evaluated practicals) to be considered in the final grade. The final grade is calculated as N = 0.50 EV1 + 0.20 EV2 + 0.30 EV3, and a minimum average of 5 out of 10 is needed to pass. If any minimum is not met, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. For extraordinary assessment, the same system applies; students must retake EV1, while EV2 and EV3 grades can be carried over or retaken, with the same minimum requirements.
